name: Dynamical systems from celestial mechanics
summary: Poincare studied orbits geometrically rather than by formulae, uncovering homoclinic phenomena in the three-body problem, and Birkhoff built on this.

name: Metric spaces (Frechet)
summary: Frechet unified earlier function-space work by Cantor, Volterra, Arzela and Hadamard into abstract metric spaces.

name: The Langlands programme: automorphic forms and Galois representations over number fields
summary: Galois representations are conjecturally matched with automorphic representations, linking arithmetic, representation theory and harmonic analysis.

name: Formal language theory
summary: Grammar types were classified by automata.

name: Frobenius method and singular ODE theory
summary: Fuchs and Frobenius used series in the complex domain to solve linear ODEs with regular singular points.

name: Euclid's Elements
summary: Results from earlier geometers were arranged as proofs from stated definitions, postulates and common notions in one treatise.

name: Boolean algebra: logic as algebra, then topology (Boole to Stone)
summary: Propositional logic is treated as an algebra, and Stone's theorem gives a topological dictionary for it, anticipating duality methods in logic and model theory.

name: Function-field Langlands: Drinfeld and Lafforgue
summary: Moduli of Drinfeld modules and shtukas, objects of algebraic geometry over finite fields, are used to prove the Langlands correspondence for function fields.

name: Murmurations: machine learning and statistics reveal patterns in elliptic curves
summary: Classifiers trained on elliptic-curve data and averages of Frobenius traces exposed oscillating patterns that were then explained for Dirichlet characters and modular forms.
